The docs were reorganized: the canonical tree is now /docs/api_reference/*, /docs/api/api-reference/*, /docs/guides/{features,routing,overview,best-practices,privacy}/*, /docs/client-sdks/*, /docs/agent-sdk/*. Several legacy /docs/features/* and /docs/api-reference/* paths still serve content, but /docs/features/tool-calling and /docs/features/reasoning-tokens return 404.

Entries with "unverified": true come from page titles in the llms.txt index (or a search-engine snippet) that were not themselves fetched; their request_surface/sdk_surface should be treated as unconfirmed.
No API keys or secrets are included.

capabilities.name: List models
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/models returns every model with id, canonical_slug, context_length, architecture (input/output modalities, tokenizer), pricing (prompt, completion, request, image, audio, web_search, internal_reasoning, input_cache_read/write), top_provider, per_request_limits, supported_parameters, default_parameters, benchmarks and alias_target. Query params include category, supported_parameters, output_modalities, sort, context, min_price/max_price, arch, providers and region.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.models.* (models sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: "output_modalities" (text, image, embeddings, audio, video, rerank, speech, transcription), "sort" (most-popular, newest, top-weekly, pricing-low-to-high ...)

capabilities.name: List endpoints for a model
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints returns each provider endpoint with pricing, quantization, context_length, max_completion_tokens, supported_parameters, status, uptime and 30-minute latency/throughput percentiles, plus supports_implicit_caching and supports_tool_choice.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.endpoints.* (endpoints sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: latency_last_30m - "Latency percentiles in milliseconds over the last 30 minutes"

capabilities.name: List models filtered by user preferences/privacy/guardrails
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists an endpoint that returns models filtered by the caller's provider preferences, privacy settings and guardrails. Path not confirmed on a fetched page.
capabilities.evidence: List models filtered by user provider preferences, privacy settings and guardrails

capabilities.name: List providers
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/providers returns provider name, slug, privacy_policy_url, terms_of_service_url, status_page_url, headquarters and datacenters country codes.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.providers.* (providers sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: headquarters - "ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code of the provider headquarters"

capabilities.name: Latest model resolution (~ prefix)
capabilities.summary: Slugs of the form ~author/family-latest (e.g. ~openai/gpt-latest, ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest) always resolve to the newest concrete model in that family; the response model field reports the concrete model used.
capabilities.evidence: ~author/family-latest slugs always resolve to the newest concrete model in a given family.

capabilities.name: Model variant suffixes
capabilities.summary: Documented variants: :free, :nitro (throughput sort + priority tier), :floor (price sort + flex tier), :online (web search), :exacto (quality-first provider sort). :thinking and :extended are documented as deprecated.
capabilities.evidence: The `:thinking` variant is deprecated and is being removed.

capabilities.name: Chat completions
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/chat/completions is the primary OpenAI-compatible endpoint; OpenRouter normalizes the schema across models and providers. Body accepts model, models, messages (or prompt), stream, sampling params, tools, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, response_format, reasoning/reasoning_effort, provider, plugins, session_id, user, prediction, service_tier, modalities, image_config, stream_options, metadata, debug, cache_control, prompt_cache_options and trace.
capabilities.evidence: OpenRouter normalizes the schema across models and providers so you only need to learn one.

capabilities.name: Prompt (non-chat) completions via prompt field
capabilities.summary: The chat completions body accepts a plain `prompt` string as an alternative to `messages`. No dedicated /api/v1/completions page was found in the current docs index.
capabilities.request_surface: POST /api/v1/chat/completions body.prompt (string; optional if messages provided)
capabilities.evidence: `prompt`: String (optional if messages provided)

capabilities.name: Anthropic Messages API compatibility
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/messages accepts Anthropic Messages format (text, images, PDFs, tools, extended thinking) with OpenRouter extensions: fallbacks (max 3), provider, plugins, session_id and openrouter:* server tools; responses add openrouter_metadata and usage.cost/is_byok.
capabilities.evidence: fallbacks: "Fallback models to try if the primary model fails or refuses, in order." Maximum of 3 entries

capabilities.name: App attribution headers
capabilities.summary: HTTP-Referer identifies the app (required for rankings); X-OpenRouter-Title (X-Title still accepted) sets the display name; X-OpenRouter-Categories assigns marketplace categories; X-OpenRouter-App-Visibility: hidden keeps a new app private.
capabilities.sdk_surface: new OpenRouter({ httpReferer, appTitle, appCategories, apiKey })
capabilities.evidence: The `HTTP-Referer` header identifies your app's URL and is used as the primary identifier for rankings.

capabilities.name: Presets
capabilities.summary: Presets are named, versioned configurations (model/models, system prompt, provider routing, parameters, tools incl. server tools) referenced via model "@preset/slug", a `preset` body field, or "model@preset/slug". They are created from request bodies via POST /api/v1/presets/{slug}/chat/completions|messages|responses.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.presets.* (presets sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: Presets are named configurations that encapsulate all the settings needed for a specific use case.

capabilities.name: Batch API (beta)
capabilities.summary: POST /api/beta/batches submits an inline array of {custom_id, body} requests for one endpoint (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages or /v1/embeddings) and model; poll GET /api/beta/batches/:id until completed, results are returned inline. Billed at 50% of standard token pricing; text-only.
capabilities.evidence: Batch requests are typically billed at 50% of the model's standard per-token pricing.

capabilities.name: Responses API
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/responses is an OpenAI-compatible, stateless Responses API supporting reasoning, tool calling, web search and streaming; requests with store: true or previous_response_id are rejected with 400. The changelog notes it graduated from beta (beta.responses is a deprecated alias).
capabilities.evidence: This API is stateless - each request is independent and no conversation state is persisted between requests.

capabilities.name: Responses API tool calling
capabilities.summary: Tools use the flat OpenAI Responses shape (type: function, name, parameters, strict); tool_choice accepts auto, none or a specific tool; parallel calls are supported; results are returned as function_call_output items keyed by call_id. Streaming emits response.output_item.added and response.function_call_arguments.done.
capabilities.evidence: Responses pair with `function_call_output` objects containing the `call_id` and result `output`

capabilities.name: Responses API reasoning
capabilities.summary: reasoning.effort (minimal/low/medium/high) controls reasoning; output includes reasoning items with encrypted_content and summary.
capabilities.evidence: Reasoning appears as a separate object type in the response array with fields: `type` (set to "reasoning"), `id`, `encrypted_content`, and `summary`.

capabilities.name: Responses API streaming events
capabilities.summary: stream: true returns SSE events response.created, response.output_item.added, response.content_part.added, response.content_part.delta, response.output_item.done, response.done, terminated by data: [DONE].
capabilities.evidence: Streaming terminates with `data: [DONE]`.

capabilities.name: SSE streaming
capabilities.summary: stream: true streams chat completions as Server-Sent Events; keep-alive comment lines (": OPENROUTER PROCESSING") must be ignored; usage arrives in the final chunk and finish_reason appears on the last content chunk and again on the usage chunk.
capabilities.evidence: Comment payload can be safely ignored per the SSE specs.

capabilities.name: Stream cancellation
capabilities.summary: Aborting the connection cancels generation and billing on providers that support it (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Fireworks, Together, DeepInfra, xAI, DeepSeek, etc.); not supported on Bedrock, Groq, Google, Mistral, Perplexity and others.
capabilities.evidence: Cancellation works by aborting the connection. Support varies by provider

capabilities.name: Mid-stream error events
capabilities.summary: Errors after the stream has started arrive as an SSE event with finish_reason: "error" and a top-level error object while the HTTP status stays 200; the stream terminates after that event.
capabilities.evidence: The HTTP status remains 200 OK, because the headers were sent before the error occurred.

capabilities.name: Client tool calling
capabilities.summary: tools follow OpenAI's function-calling shape and must be sent on every request in the loop; tool_choice accepts none, auto, required or a specific function object. Streaming accumulates tool_calls deltas until finish_reason is tool_calls.
capabilities.evidence: 'required' means the model must call one or more tools.

capabilities.name: Parallel tool calls
capabilities.summary: parallel_tool_calls (boolean, default true) lets the model emit multiple tool calls in one response; false forces one call at a time.
capabilities.evidence: When `parallel_tool_calls` is `false`, the model will only request one tool call at a time

capabilities.name: Server tools (openrouter:* tool types)
capabilities.summary: Server tools are executed by OpenRouter when the model calls them; declared in the tools array with type openrouter:web_search, openrouter:datetime, openrouter:image_generation, openrouter:web_fetch, openrouter:apply_patch, openrouter:shell, openrouter:bash, openrouter:fusion, openrouter:advisor, openrouter:subagent, openrouter:experimental__search_models and openrouter:tool_search.
capabilities.evidence: Server tools are specialized tools operated by OpenRouter that any model can call during a request.

capabilities.name: openrouter:web_search server tool
capabilities.summary: Gives any model model-decided web search (0..N searches per request) with parameters engine (auto/native/exa/firecrawl/parallel/perplexity), max_results 1-25, max_uses, max_total_results, search_context_size and allowed/excluded domains. Supersedes the deprecated web plugin which always searched once.
capabilities.evidence: The `openrouter:web_search` server tool gives any model on OpenRouter access to real-time web information.

capabilities.name: openrouter:web_fetch server tool
capabilities.summary: Lets the model fetch a URL's content; parameters engine (auto/native/exa/openrouter/firecrawl/parallel), max_uses, max_content_tokens, allowed_domains, blocked_domains. Exa and Parallel engines cost $1 per 1,000 fetches; the openrouter engine is free.
capabilities.evidence: max_uses - "Maximum fetches per request. Once exceeded, the tool returns an error"

capabilities.name: openrouter:advisor server tool
capabilities.summary: Lets a model consult a stronger advisor model mid-generation (parameters: model, instructions, forward_transcript, stream on Responses API, max_completion_tokens, reasoning). On the Messages API the type is advisor_20260301.
capabilities.evidence: The `openrouter:advisor` server tool lets a model consult a higher-intelligence advisor model mid-generation.

capabilities.name: openrouter:subagent server tool
capabilities.summary: Lets a model delegate self-contained tasks to a smaller, cheaper worker model (parameters: model, instructions, max_completion_tokens, max_tool_calls); returns status ok with outcome text or status error.
capabilities.evidence: lets a model delegate self-contained tasks to a smaller, cheaper, faster worker model mid-generation.

capabilities.name: openrouter:fusion server tool
capabilities.summary: Multi-model deliberation as a tool: a panel of 1-8 analysis_models answers in parallel and an analyst model (default: the outer model, temperature 0) returns structured JSON with consensus, contradictions, partial_coverage, unique_insights, blind_spots and raw responses. Options: max_tool_calls (1-16, default 4), max_completion_tokens (default 16000), reasoning, temperature.
capabilities.evidence: The analyst that produces the structured analysis JSON. Defaults to the same model handling your request.

capabilities.name: Sandboxed shell/bash, apply_patch, tool_search, datetime, search_models server tools
capabilities.summary: Listed on the server-tools overview: openrouter:shell (hosted sandboxed shell on Responses/Messages APIs), openrouter:bash (Anthropic-style bash), openrouter:apply_patch (V4A diffs), openrouter:tool_search (load deferred tools on demand), openrouter:datetime and openrouter:experimental__search_models. Individual pages not fetched.
capabilities.evidence: `openrouter:tool_search` - Discover and load deferred tools on demand

capabilities.name: Structured outputs (response_format json_schema)
capabilities.summary: response_format {type: json_schema, json_schema: {name, strict, schema}} enforces JSON Schema output on supporting endpoints; also supports json_object; works with streaming (valid partial JSON). Use provider.require_parameters to route only to endpoints supporting it.
capabilities.evidence: Structured outputs are also supported with streaming responses.

capabilities.name: Response Healing plugin
capabilities.summary: plugins: [{id: "response-healing"}] validates and repairs malformed JSON (missing brackets/commas/quotes, markdown fences, mixed text) for non-streaming requests that use response_format json_schema or json_object; cannot repair max_tokens truncation.
capabilities.evidence: Response Healing only applies to non-streaming requests.

capabilities.name: Provider order and allow_fallbacks
capabilities.summary: provider.order lists provider slugs to try in order (base slug matches all regions, e.g. google-vertex vs google-vertex/us-east5); provider.allow_fallbacks (default true) controls whether other providers are used when those fail.
capabilities.evidence: allow_fallbacks - "Whether to allow backup providers when the primary is unavailable"

capabilities.name: Provider filters: only, ignore, require_parameters, data_collection, quantizations, zdr
capabilities.summary: provider.only / provider.ignore allow- or deny-list provider slugs; require_parameters (default false) restricts to providers supporting every request parameter; data_collection allow|deny (default allow); quantizations filters by int4/int8/fp4/mxfp4/nvfp4/fp6/fp8/mxfp8/fp16/bf16/fp32/unknown; zdr restricts to zero-retention endpoints; enforce_distillable_text restricts to distillation-permitting models.
capabilities.sdk_surface: chat.send({ provider: { only, ignore, requireParameters, dataCollection, quantizations, zdr } })
capabilities.evidence: require_parameters - "Only use providers that support all parameters in your request"

capabilities.name: Provider sort, performance targets and max_price
capabilities.summary: Default routing load-balances across stable providers weighted by inverse square of price. provider.sort accepts "price", "throughput" or "latency", or an object {by, partition: model|none}; preferred_min_throughput / preferred_max_latency accept numbers or p50/p75/p90/p99 percentile objects over 5-minute windows; max_price caps prompt/completion/request/image pricing.
capabilities.evidence: For each model in your request, OpenRouter's default behavior is to load balance requests across providers, prioritizing price.

capabilities.name: :nitro and :floor shorthands
capabilities.summary: :nitro sorts endpoints by throughput and admits priority-tier endpoints; :floor sorts by price and admits flex-tier endpoints. Unlike service_tier, the tier is not guaranteed.
capabilities.evidence: `:nitro` sorts every endpoint for the model by throughput and admits priority tier endpoints

capabilities.name: service_tier parameter
capabilities.summary: service_tier selects flex (lower cost, ~50% discount, higher latency) or priority (fast is an alias) capacity on supporting providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex/AI Studio, xAI); the endpoint reference lists auto/default/fast/flex/priority/scale and billing follows the tier that actually served the request.
capabilities.evidence: billing follows the tier that actually served the request

capabilities.name: :exacto quality-first provider sorting
capabilities.summary: Appending :exacto makes OpenRouter prefer providers with stronger tool-calling reliability signals (real-traffic success rates, throughput/latency, harness benchmarks) instead of price-weighted ordering; it is a virtual variant with no separate endpoint pool.
capabilities.evidence: Exacto is a routing shortcut for quality-first provider ordering.

capabilities.name: Auto Exacto (default tool-calling provider optimization)
capabilities.summary: Runs by default on every tool-calling request, reordering providers by throughput, tool-calling success and benchmark data; disable by provider.sort: "price", the :floor variant, or account price sorting.
capabilities.request_surface: default behaviour on requests with body.tools; opt out via body.provider.sort="price"
capabilities.evidence: It runs by default on every tool-calling request, requiring no configuration.

capabilities.name: Router metadata (X-OpenRouter-Metadata)
capabilities.summary: Sending header X-OpenRouter-Metadata: enabled adds an openrouter_metadata object (requested, strategy, endpoints, attempts, pipeline, region, is_byok, summary) to responses; strategy values are direct, auto, free, latest, alias, fallback, pareto, bodybuilder, fusion.
capabilities.evidence: strategy: "Routing strategy used: `direct`, `auto`, `free`, `latest`, `alias`, `fallback`, `pareto`, `bodybuilder`, `fusion`"

capabilities.name: In-region routing (EU/US base URLs)
capabilities.summary: Business and Enterprise plans can send requests to https://eu.openrouter.ai or https://us.openrouter.ai so prompts and completions never leave the region (fail-closed); /api/v1/models accepts region=eu|us; guardrails can set allowed_data_regions.
capabilities.evidence: OpenRouter never silently routes a regional request outside the region.

capabilities.name: Model fallbacks (models array)
capabilities.summary: body.models lists model IDs in priority order; by default any error (context length, moderation, rate limit, downtime) triggers the next model, and the request is priced by the model actually used (returned in response.model). The Messages API equivalent `fallbacks` accepts at most 3.
capabilities.evidence: If the first model returns an error, OpenRouter will automatically try the next model in the list.

capabilities.name: Auto Router (openrouter/auto)
capabilities.summary: model: openrouter/auto classifies the prompt into ~30 task types and picks from models ranked by 7-day community spend; configurable through the auto-router plugin (costTier low/medium/high/xhigh/max, allowedModels/excludedModels wildcards, sessionId stickiness); openrouter/auto-beta uses plugin auto-beta-router. No extra fee.
capabilities.request_surface: POST /api/v1/chat/completions body.model="openrouter/auto"; body.plugins[] {id: "auto-router", costTier, allowedModels, excludedModels, sessionId}
capabilities.evidence: You pay the standard rate for whichever model is selected. There is no additional fee for using the Auto Router.

capabilities.name: Pareto code router (openrouter/pareto-code)
capabilities.summary: Routes to a coding model by minimum Artificial Analysis coding score tier (high >=0.66, medium >=0.33, low <0.33) via the pareto-router plugin, choosing the cheapest available model in the tier (or fastest with :nitro). No extra fee.
capabilities.evidence: Within the chosen tier the router selects the cheapest model that is currently available

capabilities.name: Free models router (openrouter/free)
capabilities.summary: model: openrouter/free analyzes required capabilities (vision, tools, structured outputs), filters free models that support them, and randomly selects one; the response reports which model was used.
capabilities.evidence: A model is randomly selected from the filtered pool

capabilities.name: Body Builder (openrouter/bodybuilder)
capabilities.summary: model: openrouter/bodybuilder turns a natural-language description into a JSON object {requests: [...]} of ready-to-execute OpenRouter request bodies for running the same task across several models in parallel (client executes them, e.g. with Promise.all). Free to use; system messages are preserved.
capabilities.evidence: a JSON object containing an array of OpenRouter-compatible request bodies

capabilities.name: Fusion Router (openrouter/fusion)
capabilities.summary: model: openrouter/fusion auto-injects the fusion tool: a panel (default ~anthropic/claude-opus-latest, ~openai/gpt-latest, ~google/gemini-pro-latest; 1-8 models) answers in parallel with web_search/web_fetch, then an analyst compares them and returns consensus/disagreement JSON. openrouter/fusion-flash uses the general-fast preset. Expect roughly 4-5x the cost of a single completion; the response model field reports the concrete model, and router metadata reports router: openrouter/fusion.
capabilities.request_surface: POST /api/v1/chat/completions body.model="openrouter/fusion" | body.plugins[] {id: "fusion", analysis_models, model, max_tool_calls}
capabilities.evidence: With the default 3-model panel, expect roughly 4-5x the cost of a single completion on the same prompt.

capabilities.name: Explicit prompt caching (cache_control)
capabilities.summary: Content blocks marked cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"} (optional ttl: "1h") enable provider caching on Anthropic and Alibaba Qwen (writes cost 1.25x, 2x for 1h TTL; reads 0.1x); the chat endpoint reference also lists request-level cache_control and prompt_cache_options fields.
capabilities.evidence: "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral" } with optional "ttl": "1h" for extended retention

capabilities.name: Automatic prompt caching
capabilities.summary: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google Gemini 2.5 (implicit), Grok, Groq (Kimi K2), Moonshot and Z.AI cache automatically with no configuration; cache reads are discounted 0.1x-0.5x of input price. Usage is reported in usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens and cache_discount on the generation endpoint.
capabilities.evidence: cached_tokens: "Number of tokens read from the cache (cache hit)"

capabilities.name: Provider sticky routing via session_id
capabilities.summary: OpenRouter routes follow-up requests to the same provider endpoint to maximize cache hits; session_id (max 256 chars, body or x-session-id header) is used directly as the sticky key instead of message hashing. session_id also groups requests for Broadcast traces.
capabilities.evidence: When a `session_id` is present, OpenRouter uses it directly as the sticky routing key instead of deriving one from message hashing.

capabilities.name: Response caching for identical requests
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists a Response Caching feature that caches responses for identical API requests to save time and money. Page not fetched; request surface unknown.
capabilities.evidence: Cache responses for identical API requests to save time and money

capabilities.name: plugins request array
capabilities.summary: plugins: [{id, ...options}] enables OpenRouter plugins per request; documented ids include web (deprecated in favour of the server tool), pdf, response-healing, pareto-router, context-compression, auto-router/auto-beta-router and fusion; enabled: false disables a default plugin and admins can enforce plugin config with Prevent overrides.
capabilities.evidence: "enabled": false - Disables a default plugin for a specific request

capabilities.name: Web search plugin and :online
capabilities.summary: plugins: [{id: "web"}] or the :online suffix prepends web results to any model's prompt; options max_results (default 5), search_prompt, engine (native/exa/firecrawl/parallel/perplexity), include/exclude_domains, and web_search_options.search_context_size for native search. Exa costs $0.007/request (10 results); citations return as url_citation annotations. The plugins page marks the web plugin deprecated in favour of openrouter:web_search.
capabilities.evidence: "Augment LLM responses with real-time web search results" (deprecated - use server tool instead)

capabilities.name: PDF input and file-parser engines
capabilities.summary: PDFs are sent as a content part {type: "file", file: {filename, file_data: URL or data:application/pdf;base64,...}} to any model; the pdf plugin selects engine mistral-ocr (default, $2 per 1,000 pages), cloudflare-ai (free markdown) or native (input tokens); pdf-text is deprecated and redirects to cloudflare-ai. Returned annotations carry a hash that can be sent back to skip re-parsing.
capabilities.evidence: The deprecated `pdf-text` engine automatically redirects to `cloudflare-ai`.

capabilities.name: Context compression (middle-out) plugin
capabilities.summary: plugins: [{id: "context-compression"}] removes or truncates messages from the middle of the prompt until it fits the context window; it is on by default for endpoints with <= 8k context and can be disabled with enabled: false. Claude models are additionally capped at 1,000 messages.
capabilities.evidence: All OpenRouter endpoints with 8k (8,192 tokens) or less context length will default to using context compression.

capabilities.name: Unified reasoning parameter
capabilities.summary: reasoning: {effort: max|xhigh|high|medium|low|minimal|none, max_tokens, exclude, enabled} controls thinking across models; reasoning_effort is a shorthand and include_reasoning is the legacy boolean (true = reasoning: {}, false = exclude: true).
capabilities.evidence: "include_reasoning": true -> equivalent to "reasoning": {}

capabilities.name: reasoning_details and reasoning preservation across tool calls
capabilities.summary: Responses include message.reasoning (plaintext) and message.reasoning_details (typed blocks reasoning.summary, reasoning.encrypted, reasoning.text with optional signature); sending them back on the assistant message preserves interleaved thinking across tool calls.
capabilities.request_surface: messages[] assistant.reasoning_details[] {type, id, format, index, summary|data|text, signature?}
capabilities.evidence: reasoning.encrypted - Contains "data" field with encrypted/protected reasoning

capabilities.name: Usage object (always included)
capabilities.summary: Every response (final SSE chunk when streaming) carries usage with prompt/completion/total tokens, cost, cost_details.upstream_inference_cost, prompt_tokens_details (cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens, audio_tokens, video_tokens), completion_tokens_details (reasoning_tokens, audio_tokens, image_tokens), is_byok and server_tool_use. The usage.include and stream_options.include_usage parameters are deprecated and have no effect.
capabilities.evidence: The `usage: { include: true }` and `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` parameters are deprecated and have no effect.

capabilities.name: Generation metadata endpoint
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/generation?id= returns model, provider_name, total_cost, usage, native prompt/completion/reasoning/cached token counts, generation_time, latency, moderation_latency, streamed, cancelled, finish_reason, native_finish_reason, upstream_id, is_byok, upstream_inference_cost (BYOK only), cache_discount, app_id and external_user.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.generations.* (generations sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: cache_discount - "Discount applied due to caching"

capabilities.name: Zero completion insurance
capabilities.summary: OpenRouter does not charge for responses with zero completion tokens and a blank finish reason or an error finish reason, across all models and providers; auxiliary services (web search fees, PDF OCR, web fetch) may still be billed.
capabilities.evidence: OpenRouter will not charge you for zero token responses.

capabilities.name: Generation feedback and stored content endpoints
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists endpoints to get stored prompt/completion/error content for a generation and to submit structured feedback on a generation (the MCP server exposes send-feedback). Pages not fetched.
capabilities.evidence: Submit structured feedback on a generation the authenticated user made

capabilities.name: Zero Data Retention (ZDR)
capabilities.summary: provider.zdr: true restricts routing to endpoints whose providers store no data; ZDR can also be enforced account-wide per model group or via guardrails (enforce_zdr_anthropic etc.), and the three OR together. GET /api/v1/endpoints/zdr lists ZDR endpoints; ZDR does not cover plugins/tools.
capabilities.evidence: ZDR enforcement only applies to provider routing for inference requests. It does not apply to plugins and tools

capabilities.name: Provider data policies and training opt-out
capabilities.summary: Each provider has its own retention/training policy shown in a table; opting out of training in account settings stops routing to providers that train, and provider.data_collection: "deny" applies the same restriction per request. Enterprise in-region routing keeps data in the EU or US.
capabilities.evidence: If you opt out of training in your account settings, OpenRouter will not route to providers that train.

capabilities.name: Input & Output Logging (opt-in)
capabilities.summary: An Observability setting that privately stores full prompts and completions for review on the Logs page; retained at least 3 months. A separate Data Discount Logging option gives a 1% LLM discount in exchange for data use.
capabilities.evidence: Data is retained for a minimum of 3 months, and may be retained beyond 3 months at OpenRouter's discretion

capabilities.name: Guardrails (organization controls)
capabilities.summary: Guardrails apply budget limits (daily/weekly/monthly), model and provider allowlists, regex redact/block content filters, per-model-group ZDR and allowed data regions to members or API keys; violations return HTTP 403. Managed via a /guardrails API family and the guardrails SDK sub-client.
capabilities.request_surface: guardrails API (list/create/update/delete, key and member assignments) - exact paths not fetched
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.guardrails.* (sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: When guardrails block requests, OpenRouter returns an HTTP 403 Forbidden response.

capabilities.name: Broadcast (trace export to observability platforms)
capabilities.summary: Configured under Settings > Observability, Broadcast sends request/response, token, cost, timing, model and tool-usage traces (multimodal content stripped) to 19 destinations including Langfuse, LangSmith, Datadog, BigQuery, Snowflake, S3, OTel collector and webhooks; requests can attach user, session_id and a trace metadata object (trace_id, trace_name, span_name, generation_name, parent_span_id). Destinations are also manageable via observability endpoints.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.observability.* (sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: Send traces to external observability platforms

capabilities.name: Image input
capabilities.summary: Images are sent as content parts {type: "image_url", image_url: {url}} using public URLs or data:image/...;base64 URLs; PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF are supported and multiple images can be sent as separate entries (limits vary by provider).
capabilities.evidence: Multiple images can be sent in separate content array entries

capabilities.name: Audio input and audio output in chat
capabilities.summary: Audio input uses {type: "input_audio", input_audio: {data: base64, format}} (URLs not supported; wav, mp3, aiff, aac, ogg, flac, m4a, pcm16, pcm24); audio output uses modalities: ["text","audio"] plus audio: {voice, format} and requires streaming.
capabilities.evidence: Audio files must be base64-encoded - direct URLs are not supported for audio content.

capabilities.name: Video input
capabilities.summary: Video is sent as {type: "video_url", video_url: {url}} with public URLs or base64 data URLs (mp4, mpeg, mov, webm); Gemini on AI Studio accepts YouTube links, Vertex AI does not support video URLs. Filter models by video in input_modalities.
capabilities.evidence: Google Gemini on AI Studio only supports YouTube links (not Vertex AI)

capabilities.name: Image generation API
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/images generates images (model, prompt, n 1-10, aspect_ratio, size) returning b64_json, media_type and usage.cost; GET /api/v1/images/models lists image models. The chat endpoint also accepts modalities including image and an image_config object, and openrouter:image_generation is available as a server tool.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.images.* (images sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: n - "Upper bound on images to generate (1-10)"

capabilities.name: Video generation API (async)
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/videos (model, prompt, duration, resolution, aspect_ratio, callback_url) returns a job id; poll GET /api/v1/videos/{jobId} until status completed (pending/in_progress/completed/failed) then download GET /api/v1/videos/{jobId}/content.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.videoGeneration.* (sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: Poll the polling URL (`GET /api/v1/videos/{jobId}`) until the status is `completed`

capabilities.name: Text-to-speech endpoint
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/audio/speech (model, input, voice, response_format mp3|pcm) returns a raw audio byte stream with the generation id in the X-Generation-Id header; OpenAI-SDK compatible.
capabilities.evidence: Send a `POST` request to `/api/v1/audio/speech`

capabilities.name: Speech-to-text endpoint
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions accepts JSON {model, input_audio: {data, format}, language, response_format json|verbose_json} or OpenAI-style multipart/form-data, returning transcribed text and usage.
capabilities.evidence: The endpoint also accepts OpenAI-style `multipart/form-data` requests

capabilities.name: Embeddings API
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/embeddings (model, input string/array/multimodal content with text and image_url parts, encoding_format, dimensions, provider routing) returns data[].embedding; GET /api/v1/embeddings/models lists embedding models. Embeddings are also a valid batch endpoint.
capabilities.evidence: `GET /api/v1/embeddings/models` returns available models with specifications like context length.

capabilities.name: Rerank API
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/rerank (model, query, documents as strings or {text, image} objects, top_n, provider) returns results sorted by relevance_score with the original index and document, plus usage; no streaming.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.rerank.* (rerank sub-client listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: results[].relevance_score - "Relevance score of the document to the query"

capabilities.name: Bearer API key authentication
capabilities.summary: Requests authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <key> against base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1; keys are created at openrouter.ai/keys with optional credit limits. The API has a single stable version, v1.
capabilities.evidence: Our API authenticates requests using Bearer tokens.

capabilities.name: OAuth PKCE (user-controlled API keys)
capabilities.summary: Send users to https://openrouter.ai/auth?callback_url=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256|plain (omit callback_url and set key_label for headless apps; localhost callbacks allowed on any port), then POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/keys with code, code_verifier and code_challenge_method to receive {key}. Codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes.
capabilities.evidence: Codes are "single-use and expire after 10 minutes."

capabilities.name: Workload identity federation (RFC 8693 token exchange)
capabilities.summary: OpenRouter exposes an RFC 8693 token-exchange endpoint and an RFC 7517 JWK Set for calling the API from workloads signed in with your own identity provider, without long-lived API keys; the TS SDK wraps them as oAuth.createOauthToken and oAuth.listOauthJwks. Guide page not fetched.
capabilities.request_surface: OAuth token exchange + JWKS endpoints (paths not confirmed)
capabilities.evidence: RFC 8693 token exchange for workload identity federation

capabilities.name: Management (provisioning) API keys and key CRUD
capabilities.summary: Management keys (created at settings/management-keys, cannot call completion endpoints) authorize GET/POST /api/v1/keys, GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/keys/{hash} with fields name, limit (USD), limit_reset daily|weekly|monthly, expires_at, include_byok_in_limit, disabled, creator_user_id, external, workspace_id; the plaintext key is returned once.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.apiKeys.list() / create() / get() / update() / delete() / getCurrentKeyMetadata()
capabilities.evidence: Management keys cannot be used to make API calls to OpenRouter's completion endpoints.

capabilities.name: Current key info (GET /api/v1/key)
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/key returns the calling key's limit, limit_remaining, limit_reset, usage/usage_daily/usage_weekly/usage_monthly and is_free_tier.
capabilities.evidence: `limit_remaining`: Available credits on key

capabilities.name: Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
capabilities.summary: Provider keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, ...) can be added in workspace BYOK settings or via POST /api/v1/byok; BYOK usage costs 5% of the normal OpenRouter price, deducted from credits, and responses flag usage.is_byok.
capabilities.evidence: The cost of using custom provider keys on OpenRouter is 5% of what the same model/provider would cost normally

capabilities.name: Credits endpoint
capabilities.summary: GET /api/v1/credits (management key) returns total_credits purchased and total_usage. The Coinbase Commerce crypto charge endpoint is documented as deprecated.
capabilities.evidence: total_credits: "Total credits purchased"

capabilities.name: Analytics API
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/analytics/query (management key) runs queries with metrics (e.g. request_count), up to 2 dimensions (e.g. model), time_range, granularity, filters, limit, group_limit, order_by and classifier dimensions/filters; companion endpoints return user activity by endpoint (30 days) and available metrics/dimensions.
capabilities.evidence: dimensions - "Dimension to group by (up to 2)"

capabilities.name: Rate limits
capabilities.summary: Free (:free) models are limited to 20 RPM and 50 RPD (1,000 RPD after buying >= $10 of credits); platform 429s include X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset headers, upstream 429s carry error.metadata.provider_code and trigger fallback; negative balances yield 402 even on free models.
capabilities.evidence: If your account has a negative credit balance, you may see 402 errors, including for free models.

capabilities.name: Error response shape and status codes
capabilities.summary: Errors return {error: {code, message, metadata?}}; codes 400 bad request, 401 invalid credentials, 402 insufficient credits, 403 forbidden/guardrail/moderation, 408 timeout, 429 rate limited, 502 model down/invalid response, 503 no provider meets routing requirements. Moderation metadata includes reasons, flagged_input, provider_name, model_slug; provider errors include error_type and provider_code.
capabilities.evidence: 503: "There is no available model provider that meets your routing requirements"

capabilities.name: OpenAPI spec, single v1 version and changelog
capabilities.summary: The API is a single stable version v1 with breaking changes (removals, renames, type changes, nullability widening) documented in the changelog with migration guidance; the spec is published at https://openrouter.ai/openapi.json and openapi.yaml and the client SDKs are auto-generated from it.
capabilities.evidence: The OpenRouter API has a single stable version, `v1`, selected by the URL path

capabilities.name: OpenRouter MCP server
capabilities.summary: A hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.openrouter.ai/mcp (OAuth; issues a 7-day, $10-limit API key) exposes 15 tools: send-message, generate-image, send-feedback, list-models, get-model, list-model-endpoints, list-providers, list-daily-model-rankings, list-app-rankings, get-credits, get-generation, list-benchmarks, list-task-classifications, search-docs, spawn-ori-eval, install-ori-harness and ping.
capabilities.evidence: The issued token is a standard OpenRouter API key labeled `OpenRouter MCP: <app name>`

capabilities.name: Ori Eval (LLM judge for model comparison)
capabilities.summary: Ori is OpenRouter's CLI (install via https://openrouter.ai/labs/ori/install.sh) that runs your agent harness against candidate models through OpenRouter; evals can score answers with an LLM judge created by setupJudge(), which runs on a separate grading model. This is the only documented use of the word 'judge' as an API concept.
capabilities.evidence: The `setupJudge()` function makes a separate agent on its own grading model.

capabilities.name: judge_model deprecated alias (Fusion streaming event)
capabilities.summary: The July 28, 2026 changelog entry renames the Fusion streaming event field: FusionCallAnalysisInProgressEvent gained a required analyst_model property that replaces judge_model, with judge_model retained as a deprecated alias.
capabilities.evidence: `analyst_model` replaces `judge_model`... `judge_model` is retained as a deprecated alias

capabilities.name: Workspaces, files and containers APIs
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists workspace management (CRUD, budgets, members), a Files API (upload, list, get metadata, download, delete files referenced in later calls) and container file endpoints for the shell/bash sandboxes. Pages not fetched.
capabilities.sdk_surface: openRouter.workspaces.* / openRouter.files.* (sub-clients listed in TS SDK index)
capabilities.evidence: Uploads a file to be referenced in future API calls

capabilities.name: Benchmarks, datasets and task-classification endpoints
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists a unified benchmarks endpoint, public usage datasets (top apps, daily token totals, cost-per-session) and a task-classification market-share endpoint, mirrored by benchmarks/datasets/classifications SDK sub-clients. Pages not fetched.
capabilities.evidence: Unified benchmark endpoint that aggregates scores from multiple benchmark sources

capabilities.name: @openrouter/sdk package
capabilities.summary: @openrouter/sdk (npm latest 1.2.107, ESM-only, depends on zod ^3.25||^4) is auto-generated from the OpenAPI spec alongside the Python (openrouter) and Go (go-sdk) SDKs; it exposes chat, responses, models, endpoints, generations, credits, apiKeys, analytics, embeddings, images, videoGeneration, tts, stt, byok, files, guardrails, observability, organization, presets, providers, rerank, workspaces, benchmarks, classifications, datasets and oauth sub-clients.
capabilities.evidence: All three SDKs are auto-generated from the OpenRouter OpenAPI spec

capabilities.name: chat.send with streaming and provider options
capabilities.summary: openRouter.chat.send({ messages, model, provider: { zdr, sort }, stream }) returns a response or, with stream: true, an async iterable of chunks; the README also documents paginated async iteration (byok.list()) and multipart file uploads.
capabilities.evidence: provider: { zdr: true, sort: "price" }, stream: true

capabilities.name: Client constructor options (apiKey, httpReferer, appTitle, appCategories)
capabilities.summary: The SDK examples construct new OpenRouter({ httpReferer, appTitle, appCategories, apiKey }) which map to the attribution headers; per-call RequestOptions accept fetchOptions and retries (RetryConfig). A standalone-function form (OpenRouterCore + creditsGetCredits) is also generated.
capabilities.sdk_surface: new OpenRouter({ apiKey, httpReferer, appTitle, appCategories }); options.retries: RetryConfig
capabilities.evidence: const openRouter = new OpenRouter({ httpReferer: "<value>", appTitle: "<value>", appCategories: "<value>", apiKey: ... })

capabilities.name: SDK DevTools (telemetry capture)
capabilities.summary: The docs index lists SDK Development Tools for telemetry capture and visualization for both the client SDK and the Agent SDK. Page not fetched.
capabilities.evidence: SDK Development Tools for telemetry capture and visualization

capabilities.name: @openrouter/agent package (callModel moved here)
capabilities.summary: callModel, tool, stop conditions, async params, conversation-state helpers and message-format converters moved from @openrouter/sdk to the standalone @openrouter/agent package (npm latest 0.11.0; deps zod ^4 and @openrouter/sdk; optional peer @modelcontextprotocol/client ^2); the old exports will be removed from @openrouter/sdk in a future major. Python (openrouter-agent-sdk) and Go ports exist.
capabilities.evidence: `callModel` and its associated types have moved to the `@openrouter/agent` package.

capabilities.name: callModel inference loop
capabilities.summary: callModel({ model | models, input, instructions, tools, stopWhen, allowFinalResponse, parallelToolCalls, temperature, maxOutputTokens, topP, topK, toolChoice, reasoning, provider, metadata, context, hooks, signal }) runs a multi-turn loop with automatic tool execution; the ModelResult exposes getText(), getResponse(), getToolCalls(), getReasoning() and streaming accessors plus cancel(). maxToolRounds is deprecated.
capabilities.evidence: A unified API for calling any LLM with automatic tool execution and multiple consumption patterns

capabilities.name: tool() with Zod schemas
capabilities.summary: tool({ name, description, inputSchema: z.object(...), outputSchema, execute: async (params, context) => ..., onToolCalled }) defines typed tools; execute may be false for manual handling, context exposes numberOfTurns, turnRequest, toolCall and setContext(), and generator tools stream progress via getToolStream().
capabilities.sdk_surface: tool({ name, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute, onToolCalled, nextTurnParams })
capabilities.evidence: `execute`: function or `false` - execution logic (required unless using `onToolCalled`)

capabilities.name: stopWhen stop conditions
capabilities.summary: stopWhen accepts stepCountIs(n), hasToolCall(name), maxTokensUsed(n), maxCost(usd), finishReasonIs(reason), an array (stops when any condition is met) or a custom ({steps}) => boolean function; without stopWhen the loop runs until a turn has no tool calls, and allowFinalResponse controls the closing text turn.
capabilities.evidence: If `stopWhen` is not specified, the loop runs until the model produces a turn with no tool calls.

capabilities.name: nextTurnParams (tools that change the next turn)
capabilities.summary: A tool's nextTurnParams map of parameterName: (params, context) => value rewrites callModel parameters (model, temperature, instructions, input, maxOutputTokens, topP, topK) for the following turn; they run after all execute functions, in tools-array order.
capabilities.evidence: Tools can modify any `callModel` parameter for the next turn.

capabilities.name: Dynamic (function-valued) parameters
capabilities.summary: Any callModel parameter (model, instructions, temperature, maxOutputTokens, provider, ...) can be a sync or async function of TurnContext {numberOfTurns, turnRequest, toolCall}, enabling per-turn model switching or instruction building.
capabilities.evidence: Any parameter in `callModel` can be a function that computes its value based on conversation context.

capabilities.name: Streaming consumption patterns
capabilities.summary: ModelResult offers getTextStream(), getReasoningStream(), getItemsStream() (recommended; yields complete items by id: message, function_call, reasoning, web_search_call, file_search_call, image_generation_call, function_call_output), getFullResponsesStream() (all events incl. tool.preliminary_result / tool.result), getToolCallsStream() and getToolStream(); getNewMessagesStream() is deprecated.
capabilities.evidence: Each iteration yields a complete item with the same ID but updated content. Replace items by ID rather than accumulating deltas.

capabilities.name: Message format converters
capabilities.summary: fromChatMessages() and fromClaudeMessages() convert OpenAI-chat or Anthropic-style message arrays into OpenResponses input; toChatMessage() and toClaudeMessage() convert an OpenResponses response back. No toResponsesAPI/toAISDK/toCompletionsAPI/toDeltas helpers are documented.
capabilities.evidence: Convert OpenAI chat-style messages to OpenResponses input

capabilities.name: Remote MCP servers as callModel tools
capabilities.summary: createMCPTools({ url, transport: streamableHttp|sse, auth: bearer|headers|oauth, includeTools, excludeTools }) connects a remote MCP server and returns tools to spread into callModel; close the handle when done. Targets HTTP servers, not stdio.
capabilities.sdk_surface: const mcp = await createMCPTools({ url, auth }); callModel({ tools: [...mcp.tools] })
capabilities.evidence: Call `createMCPTools()` once, spread `mcp.tools` into `callModel`, and close the handle when you're done

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks (HooksManager)
capabilities.summary: Built-in hooks SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostModelCall, PermissionRequest, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop and SessionEnd let you observe, rewrite or block steps (hooks.on(name, { matcher, handler })); custom hooks are declared with Zod payload/result schemas and emitted via hooks.emit().
capabilities.sdk_surface: new HooksManager({...}); hooks.on("PreToolUse", { matcher, handler }); callModel({ hooks })
capabilities.evidence: PreToolUse - "Before client tool execution" - rewrite or block tools

capabilities.name: Human-in-the-loop approval, async tools and doom-loop detection
capabilities.summary: onToolCalled on a tool returns a value to auto-respond or null to pause for approval; the docs index also lists tool approval state persistence, async/background tools deferred to external systems, and doom-loop detection for repeated tool calls (those three pages were not fetched).
capabilities.evidence: `onToolCalled`: HITL hook - "return value to auto-respond, `null` to pause"
